scope: Independently authored unrotated default rectangle, triangle and diamond anchors with opaque RGB fill and no stroke in ordinary managed output. No group, adjustment, alternative-description output or live Word behavior is established by this working-tree observation.
provenance: Synthetic python-docx 1.2.0 (MIT) documents with independently authored DrawingML and normalized ZIP metadata. All three inputs regenerated byte for byte. Open XML SDK 3.5.1 reported zero errors for all source and saved documents; validator DLL SHA-256 4126071233c70310683c0fa0b65648bbd34839afa7b0a2309fba13c22501ddec.
observations: PyMuPDF 1.27.2.2 independently checked the colored PDF polygons against the authored vertices and edges in WordNet and LibreOffice output. SVG vertices were exact and XPS coordinates were checked after converting 96-dpi units to points. There were no raster images. The check rejected a changed editable preset and a substituted reference polygon; the changed DOCX SHA-256 is a0b2a44baa0fff0a91001935235fe926572f26a00da207f5e9296a236fd340b9.
referenceTool: LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 ran with network disabled in image sha256:a3aaef646226d406fc2b511462beb0359f4cd8859d775f404bd8f137dfd5f644.
retainedEarlierAttempts: The first focused build had a nullable options error and omitted a required conversion-options argument; both test calls were corrected. The first focused execution attempted unsupported DOCX-to-DOCX conversion and failed four cases; the tests now use an editable WordDocument session. An early independent probe used Strict preview with python-docx's theme references and failed Docx.ThemeFont; the final probe explicitly uses BestEffort and preserves the theme diagnostic.
limitations: Generated documents, PDFs, XPS and SVG remain scratch artifacts. Exact-commit, package and hosted runtime evidence are separate. Arrow presets, adjustments, rotations, groups, gradients, authored alternative semantics in non-DOCX output, tagged/archive/native combinations and complete #161 qualification remain open.
